Summary  
Data source overview: The post argues that the long-term suffering of farmed animals could reach astronomical scales because factory farming—especially of fish and invertebrates—may persist on Earth and even spread through space with help from AI technologies. It claims that individual diet both shapes and signals values that flow through EA and AI-safety communities into technical and governance choices affecting whether that risk materialises.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[82]  
Inference strategy justification: The author offers qualitative reasoning rather than formal models; I extracted every distinct claim that links the stated risk to concrete levers (dietary change, alignment objective design, AI governance, research agenda). Moderate inference (confidence 2) was applied when connecting valuation bias and research needs that were implicit but strongly suggested.  
Extraction completeness explanation: All causal-interventional chains present in Parts 1-4 were decomposed into 21 tightly-granular nodes and 22 edges with no orphans, covering technical, social and governance mechanisms. Framework-level ideas (e.g. “value signalling”) were explicitly broken into white-box components.  
Key limitations: The source provides limited empirical evidence, so many edge confidences are medium or weak. Interventions are high-level and may overlap with broader literature; future cross-source merging will need synonym handling.
